definitions.explanation: An organized group of musicians who perform together. Can refer to a symphony orchestra, a jazz band, a military band, or other musical ensembles.

examples.japanese: この{楽団|がくだん}は{毎年|まいとし}{定期|ていき}{演奏会|えんそうかい}を{開|ひら}いている。
examples.english: This orchestra holds regular concerts every year.

examples.japanese: {世界的|せかいてき}に{有名|ゆうめい}な{楽団|がくだん}が{来日|らいにち}し、{各地|かくち}で{公演|こうえん}を{行|おこな}った。
examples.english: A world-famous orchestra came to Japan and gave performances in various cities.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{楽|がく} (music) + {団|だん} (group, troupe). Literally "music group."

USAGE:
{楽団|がくだん} is the general Japanese term for an organized musical group. More specific terms exist: {管弦楽団|かんげんがくだん} (symphony orchestra), {吹奏楽団|すいそうがくだん} (wind ensemble), {軍楽隊|ぐんがくたい} (military band). オーケストラ (orchestra) is also commonly used for Western-style orchestras.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {交響|こうきょう}{楽団|がくだん}: symphony orchestra
- {管弦|かんげん}{楽団|がくだん}: orchestra (lit. wind and string ensemble)
- {楽団|がくだん}の{指揮者|しきしゃ}: conductor of an orchestra
- {楽団|がくだん}{員|いん}: orchestra member
- {楽団|がくだん}を{率|ひき}いる: to lead an orchestra
